topic: Indian dams and reservoirs — mixed tiers
description: Bhakra Nangal, Tehri, Sardar Sarovar, Hirakud, Nagarjuna Sagar, Mettur, Idukki, Koyna, Tungabhadra

questions.stem: The Bhakra-Nangal Dam, India's first major multipurpose project after Independence, is built on the:

options.option_text: Beas
Sutlej (between Himachal Pradesh and Punjab)
Yamuna
Ravi

questions.explanation: Bhakra-Nangal — Sutlej. Bhakra Dam: 226 m high (one of the tallest gravity dams in the world); Govind Sagar reservoir behind it (named after Sikh guru Gobind Singh). Nangal Dam — downstream of Bhakra, smaller, regulates flow. Inaugurated 1963 by Pt Nehru — called it a 'temple of modern India'. Benefits Punjab + Haryana + Rajasthan + HP (irrigation + hydropower). Capacity: 1,325 MW. Managed by BBMB (Bhakra-Beas Management Board). Beas — Pong Dam (HP). Yamuna — Tehri (no, Tehri is on Bhagirathi); on Yamuna there's Hathnikund Barrage. Ravi — Thein/Ranjit Sagar Dam.

questions.stem: The Tehri Dam — India's TALLEST dam at 260.5 m — is built on which river?

options.option_text: Alaknanda
Bhagirathi (a head-stream of the Ganga, in Uttarakhand)
Yamuna
Mandakini

questions.explanation: Tehri Dam — Bhagirathi River, Uttarakhand. Height 260.5 m (TALLEST dam in India; among the top 10 highest in the world). Earth + rock-fill type. Capacity 2,400 MW (one of India's largest hydropower complexes, includes Tehri pumped storage). Submerged the old Tehri town + 100+ villages — major displacement controversy in the 1980s-90s. The Bhagirathi merges with the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. Five Prayags (sacred confluences) along the Ganga's headwaters: Devprayag, Rudraprayag, Karnaprayag, Nandaprayag, Vishnuprayag. Mandakini joins at Rudraprayag.

questions.stem: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, the world's tallest masonry dam at the time of construction, is built across the:

options.option_text: Godavari
Krishna (in Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border, Nalgonda + Guntur districts)
Cauvery
Tungabhadra

questions.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam — Krishna river, on the AP-Telangana border (post-2014 bifurcation). Height 124 m, length 1,550 m. Inaugurated 1967 (Indira Gandhi). Largest masonry dam in the world at the time. Reservoir Nagarjuna Sagar (~11 km³ live capacity). Named after Nagarjuna, the 2nd-century Buddhist scholar; the nearby site Nagarjunakonda is an important Buddhist archaeological site (now an island in the reservoir; relics relocated). Generates 815 MW + irrigates ~10 lakh hectares. Krishna's other major projects: Srisailam (upstream of Nagarjuna Sagar), Almatti, Tungabhadra (on tributary). Cauvery — Mettur Dam, Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS).

questions.stem: The Sardar Sarovar Dam, on the Narmada river, is located in which state and benefits FOUR states?

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh; benefits MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan
Gujarat; benefits Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan
Maharashtra; benefits Maharashtra, MP, Goa, Karnataka
Rajasthan; benefits Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana

questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam — at Kevadia in Gujarat (Narmada district). 4-state beneficiary project: Gujarat (largest share), Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan. Cleared by Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal (1979). Foundation stone Pt Nehru 1961; full height (138.7 m) attained 2017; inaugurated by PM Modi on his 67th birthday (17 Sep 2017). Statue of Unity (Sardar Patel, 182 m, world's tallest statue) — adjacent to the dam, dedicated 31 Oct 2018. Movement against displacement: Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar, Baba Amte, Arundhati Roy). Power 1,450 MW. Other Narmada dams: Indira Sagar (MP), Omkareshwar (MP).

questions.stem: The Mettur Dam, one of the oldest dams in India (built 1934), is on the:

options.option_text: Krishna river, Andhra Pradesh
Cauvery (Kaveri) river, Tamil Nadu
Tapi river, Maharashtra
Periyar river, Kerala

questions.explanation: Mettur Dam (also known as Stanley Reservoir) — Kaveri/Cauvery river, Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Built 1934, ~215 m crest length. Inaugurated by Sir George Frederick Stanley (then Acting Governor of Madras Presidency). Major irrigation source for the Kaveri delta. Other Cauvery dams — Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS, Karnataka, Mandya district, 1932); Kabini (in Karnataka); Banasura Sagar (Kerala). Cauvery water dispute — KARNATAKA vs TAMIL NADU (with Kerala + Puducherry as parties); long-running, settled in stages by tribunal + SC; Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) constituted 2018.

questions.stem: The Idukki Dam, in Kerala — Asia's first arch dam — is built across the:

options.option_text: Pamba
Periyar (largest river of Kerala)
Bharathapuzha
Chaliyar

questions.explanation: Idukki Dam — Periyar river, Kerala (Idukki district). Built 1976. ASIA'S FIRST + INDIA'S FIRST arch (double-curvature) dam. Height 168 m. Construction support from Canada (CIDA). Generates 780 MW (largest hydro project in Kerala). Built between two granite hills — Kuravan + Kurathi. Periyar — 244 km, longest river of Kerala (also called the 'lifeline' of Kerala). Periyar National Park / Tiger Reserve also in this basin. Pamba — sacred river (Sabarimala). Bharathapuzha — 'Nila', second longest. Chaliyar — Kozhikode area. Other Kerala dams: Mullaperiyar (controversial, with Tamil Nadu, on the Periyar headwaters in Kerala but operated by TN since 1886 lease).

questions.stem: Match the following dams with their states/rivers — pick the WRONG pairing:

options.option_text: Hirakud — Mahanadi — Odisha
Koyna — Krishna — Maharashtra
Tungabhadra — Tungabhadra — Karnataka
Rihand — Rihand (Sone tributary) — UP

questions.explanation: Koyna is on the KOYNA river (a tributary of the Krishna), in Maharashtra — NOT directly on the Krishna. Largest hydro project of Maharashtra (2,000 MW). Located in Satara district. The 1967 Koyna earthquake (M 6.6) was a famous 'reservoir-induced seismicity' case. Other matches verify: HIRAKUD (Mahanadi, Odisha — world's longest earthen dam, 1957). TUNGABHADRA (Tungabhadra, Karnataka — built 1953, joint AP-Karnataka). RIHAND (Rihand river, a Sone tributary; UP-Sonbhadra district; reservoir is Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar).

questions.stem: The Hirakud Dam — the world's longest earthen dam at approximately 25.8 km — is built across which river in Odisha?

options.option_text: Brahmani river, originating in Jharkhand's Chota Nagpur plateau
Mahanadi river, forming a vast reservoir near Sambalpur district
Baitarani river, which drains into the Bay of Bengal near Jajpur
Rushikulya river, originating in the Eastern Ghats of southern Odisha

questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi river near Sambalpur, Odisha, completed in 1957. It is the world's longest earthen dam. Brahmani and Baitarani are also Odisha rivers but are unconnected to Hirakud; the Rushikulya is a minor southern Odisha coastal river.

questions.stem: Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar — India's largest reservoir by surface area (~465 sq km) — is created by which dam?

options.option_text: Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi river in Odisha state
Rihand Dam on the Rihand river in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh
Indira Sagar Dam on the Narmada river in Madhya Pradesh
Srisailam Dam on the Krishna river in Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: The Rihand Dam (completed 1962) on the Rihand river in Sonbhadra, UP, creates the Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar — India's largest reservoir by surface area. Indira Sagar (Narmada, MP) surpasses it in live storage capacity but not surface area; this distinction frequently confuses candidates.

questions.stem: The 1967 Koynanagar earthquake (magnitude ~6.5), a landmark case of reservoir-induced seismicity studied globally, is linked to the filling of which dam's reservoir?

options.option_text: Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh
Koyna Dam on the Koyna river in the Sahyadri range, Maharashtra
Tungabhadra Dam on the Tungabhadra river in Karnataka
Srisailam Dam on the Krishna river in Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: Koyna Dam in Maharashtra is the world's most cited example of reservoir-triggered seismicity — the 1967 earthquake killed ~200 people and is attributed to the stress changes caused by impounding the Shivajisagar reservoir. Bhakra and Srisailam are also large reservoirs but are not linked to this event.

questions.stem: Which dam on the Narmada river holds India's single largest live storage capacity (~12.22 billion cubic metres), located near Punasa in Khandwa district?

options.option_text: Sardar Sarovar Dam, located at Navagam village in Gujarat
Indira Sagar Dam, located near Punasa in Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh
Bargi Dam, the first completed dam built on the Narmada river
Omkareshwar Dam, sited just downstream of the Indira Sagar project

questions.explanation: Indira Sagar Dam (completed 2005) at Punasa, Madhya Pradesh, is India's largest reservoir by live storage capacity. Sardar Sarovar on the same Narmada river is taller and politically prominent, making it a common wrong pick, but its live storage (~5.8 BCM) is far smaller than Indira Sagar's.

questions.stem: The Tungabhadra Dam is an inter-state joint project managed by a special board — it primarily serves irrigation and hydropower needs of which two states?

options.option_text: Karnataka and Maharashtra, linked through the upper Bhima sub-basin
Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, sharing Tungabhadra river waters jointly
Telangana and Karnataka, under the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal
Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, as part of Godavari basin allocation

questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra Dam at Hospet (Karnataka) was a joint project of the erstwhile Hyderabad and Mysore states; post-reorganisation it serves Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh (now including Telangana after bifurcation). Telangana is often chosen instead of Andhra Pradesh since bifurcation, but the original bilateral board covers both successor AP states collectively.

questions.stem: The Baglihar hydroelectric project on the Chenab river was contested by Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty 1960 — which neutral expert gave binding recommendations in 2007, largely upholding India's design?

options.option_text: Salman Salman, a World Bank water-law specialist based in Washington
Raymond Lafitte, a Swiss civil engineer appointed by the World Bank
John Briscoe, a Harvard professor designated as court-of-arbitration chair
Peter Gleick, a Pacific Institute hydrologist engaged via UNEP mediation

questions.explanation: Raymond Lafitte, a Swiss engineer, was appointed Neutral Expert by the World Bank and issued his final determination in February 2007, directing India to make minor modifications (freeboard, pondage) but broadly validating the dam's design. John Briscoe is a real Harvard water expert but had no adjudicative role at Baglihar; Salman and Gleick are plausible distractors drawn from IWT academic literature.

questions.stem: The Polavaram multipurpose project on the Godavari river in Andhra Pradesh is designated a National Project under Article 14 of the River Boards Act — its submergence zone extends into which two other states, requiring their statutory consent?

options.option_text: Telangana and Maharashtra, as upper Godavari originates in their territory
Chhattisgarh and Odisha, whose tribal forest lands fall in the flood zone
Maharashtra and Telangana, covered under the Godavari Disputes Tribunal award
Odisha and Maharashtra, included explicitly in Polavaram's EIA notification

questions.explanation: Polavaram's full reservoir level (FRL 45.72 m) submerges forest and tribal (Schedule V) villages in Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Both states' consent is legally required, and their opposition has periodically delayed the project. Telangana (post-bifurcation) also has concerns, but Chhattisgarh and Odisha are the two states with formally notified submergence areas — the distinction examiners probe.
